sources.title: How to Help Your Child Develop Empathy
sources.publisher: Zero To Three (page dated 1 Feb 2016)
sources.quote: We often insist that our toddlers say "I'm sorry" as a way for them to take responsibility for their actions. ... it doesn't necessarily help toddlers learn empathy. ... help children focus on the other person's feelings. ... Developing empathy takes time. ... Kayla is feeling sad because you took her toy car. ... Read stories about feelings.
sources.supports: Insisting on 'sorry' does not necessarily build empathy in toddlers; help children focus on the other person's feelings by naming them; empathy takes time; reading stories about feelings is recommended. Written for toddlers; we apply it to ages 3 to 5 as an analogy.

sources.title: Toddlers and Challenging Behavior: Why They Do It and How to Respond
sources.publisher: Zero To Three (page dated 29 Feb 2020)
sources.quote: Toddlers who are asked to say “sorry” without fully understanding what they’ve done wrong, do not learn from their actions. ... It helps when parents model how to apologize and take responsibility for their actions too.
sources.supports: Asking a toddler to say sorry without understanding what they did does not teach from the action; parents modelling apologies helps. Written for toddlers; applied to ages 3 to 5 as an analogy.

sources.title: Forcing kids to say 'I'm sorry' doesn't fool anybody
sources.publisher: Futurity, reporting a University of Michigan study (Craig Smith et al., Merrill-Palmer Quarterly, children aged 4 to 9), 30 Nov 2018
sources.quote: Coercing your child to apologize is going to backfire. ... But the coerced apologies weren't seen as effective, especially by the 7-to-9-year-olds, Smith says. ... "When your child is calm, help them see how the other person is feeling, and why," Smith says. "Research shows that even preschoolers value it when a wrongdoer makes amends with action."
sources.supports: In a study of children, coerced apologies were seen as less effective (especially by ages 7 to 9); the researcher advises waiting until the child is calm and helping them see how the other person feels; preschoolers value amends made with action. The study measured children's judgments, not long-term outcomes.

sources.title: Taming Tempers
sources.publisher: Nemours KidsHealth (reviewed June 2022, Margaux J. Barnes, PhD)
sources.quote: Once your child calms down, ask what got them so upset. ... But don't push too hard for your child to talk right then. ... They may need some time to reflect before being ready to talk.
sources.supports: After an outburst wait until the child calms down before talking; they may need time to reflect before being ready to talk. The page is about tempers, applied here to the moment after a conflict.

sources.supports: Children are often taught to say sorry without naming what happened; a full apology names the specific wrong; parents can model full apologies.

sources.title: Forcing kids to say 'I'm sorry' doesn't fool anybody
sources.publisher: Futurity, reporting a University of Michigan study (Craig Smith et al., Merrill-Palmer Quarterly, children aged 4 to 9), 30 Nov 2018
sources.quote: Coercing your child to apologize is going to backfire. ... But the coerced apologies weren't seen as effective, especially by the 7-to-9-year-olds, Smith says. ... "When your child is calm, help them see how the other person is feeling, and why," Smith says. "Research shows that even preschoolers value it when a wrongdoer makes amends with action."
sources.supports: In a study of children, coerced apologies were seen as less effective (especially by ages 7 to 9); the researcher advises waiting until the child is calm and helping them see how the other person feels; preschoolers value amends made with action. The study measured children's judgments, not long-term outcomes.

claims.wording_he: 9 דרכים שכן מלמדות
claims.supports: The hook quotes a parent's worry (in quotation marks, not a claim). The nine ways are our practical list; each rests on a source named on its own slide: Zero To Three, the American Academy of Pediatrics and the Michigan researcher via Futurity.

claims.wording_he: אם הוא לא מבין למה סליחה לא מלמדת לפי ארגון אמריקאי לגיל הרך
claims.supports: Zero To Three: toddlers who are asked to say sorry without fully understanding what they have done wrong do not learn from their actions. Written for toddlers; applied to ages 3 to 5 as an analogy.

claims.wording_he: ולכן תתחילו מלהבין מה קרה
claims.supports: Our reading of the same source: if understanding is what is missing, the ways that follow start from understanding what happened and how the other child feels.

claims.wording_he: מדברים על זה רק כשהוא רגוע
claims.supports: The Michigan researcher via Futurity: when your child is calm, help them see how the other person is feeling, and why.

claims.wording_he: נסו עשר שניות נשימה ביחד
claims.supports: Practical suggestion of ours for getting to calm; rests only on the researcher's advice to wait until the child is calm. No source tests breathing.

claims.wording_he: רון לקחת לה את המכונית
claims.supports: Imagined sentence to say; rests on AAP (children are often taught to say sorry without naming what happened) and the Zero To Three example about taking a toy car.

claims.wording_he: היא עצובה כי המכונית שלה / רון תסתכל על הפנים שלה
claims.supports: Zero To Three: help children focus on the other person's feelings (example: Kayla is feeling sad because you took her toy car); the Michigan researcher: help them see how the other person is feeling, and why. The sentences are our wording; looking at the face is our practical suggestion.

claims.wording_he: להתנצל לפניו: סליחה שצעקתי עליך התעצבנתי על הבלגן
claims.supports: Zero To Three: it helps when parents model how to apologize and take responsibility; AAP: model full apologies that name the specific wrong (its example: I am sorry I yelled at you, Mommy felt frustrated with the mess).

claims.wording_he: לתת לו לתקן: מה נעשה עכשיו כדי שיהיה לה טוב
claims.supports: The researcher says preschoolers value it when a wrongdoer makes amends with action; the advice to let him choose how to fix it and the sentence are ours. The study measured children's judgments, not long-term outcomes.

claims.wording_he: אמפתיה לוקחת זמן
claims.supports: Zero To Three: developing empathy takes time. Written for toddlers; applied to ages 3 to 5 as an analogy.

claims.wording_he: גם אם הפעם הוא שותק
claims.supports: Possibility for this one child, not a claim about children; rests on empathy taking time.

claims.wording_he: סליחה נלמדת מהבנה ולא מכפייה
claims.supports: Our summing up of the slides before it; rests on Zero To Three (apology without understanding does not teach) and the Michigan study (coerced apologies seen as less effective).

claims.wording_he: אפשר לעזור לו גם בסיפור אישי
claims.supports: Zero To Three recommends reading stories about feelings. That the story is personalised, with the child as the hero, is our wording.

claims.wording_he: ספר שבו הילד שלכם הוא הגיבור
claims.supports: The child's name is in the text and he stars in every illustration (live site FAQ, 13 Oct 2026). No brand or title on the slide.

versions.conversion_rationale: ההבטחה בכריכה היא מספר וערך (9 דרכים) והחשש של ההורה מצוטט במילים שלו. שקופית 2 מסבירה למה כפייה לא מלמדת, שקופיות 3 עד 8 נותנות תשע דרכים ממוספרות עם משפט להגיד, שקופית 9 מסכמת לצילום מסך, ושקופית 10 מציעה סיפור אישי כצעד טבעי הבא.
